name: Ca Mau food guide
summary: Ca Mau eats the mangrove: crab for the meal, salted ba khía with hot rice, and dried shrimp, Năm Căn crackers, and U Minh honey to carry home. The forest day adds grilled snakehead, bee-pupa salad, and eel braised with nhàu leaves.
body: Eat Cà Mau as the cape, not as a second Cần Thơ. The plate that tells you where you are is mangrove crab, or ba khía muối with hot rice. Mudskipper and Khai Long clams come from the same flats, and the U Minh forest brings the fermented-fish hotpot, grilled snakehead, bee pupae, and eel.

The U Minh hotpot has two published recipes. One cooks it with mắm cá sặc, lemongrass, fish, shrimp, squid, and forest greens. Another cooks it with mắm sặt, freshwater fish, coconut water, and a green list that includes hẹ nước.
Eat by area rather than by restaurant: crab at Đất Mũi and in the city, ba khía at Rạch Gốc, the forest plates at U Minh Hạ. The river market on the Gành Hào is the city's food scene on the water.
specialtiesLead: Crab and salted ba khía lead. Then the mangrove flats, the U Minh forest, and the dried bags to carry home.

sections.heading: Where to eat
paragraphs: Đất Mũi and the city are the crab. Rạch Gốc is the ba khía. U Minh Hạ is the hotpot, the grilled snakehead, the honey, the bee-pupa salad, and the eel. Năm Căn is the cracker and the boats on the way south. Cái Đôi Vàm is the dried cá khoai. Cái Nước is the bồn bồn. Thới Bình is the fermented snakehead.
Order by the area and the dish rather than by a restaurant name.

sections.heading: Food streets and markets
paragraphs: UNESCO describes a floating market of hundreds of boats on the Gành Hào, in the center of Cà Mau city. Come to move among the produce boats, or watch from the bank. This is not the Cần Thơ dawn.
Rạch Gốc is the town where the salted crab gets its name. Eat ba khía there with hot rice on the way to the cape.

spots.name: Ca Mau floating market
spots.note: Boats loaded with produce on the Gành Hào, in the middle of the city. Move among them by boat or watch from the bank.

spots.name: Rach Goc
spots.address: Khóm 8, thị trấn Rạch Gốc, huyện Ngọc Hiển in the 2024 culture-office listing; later cape listings say xã Đất Mũi.
spots.note: The town of the salted mangrove crab. Eat ba khía muối with hot rice on the cape day.

sections.heading: Plates
paragraphs: Start with cua Cà Mau and ba khía muối. On 24 October 2020 the crab is also called cua Năm Căn and is exported to Korea, Malaysia, China, and Taiwan. A workshop of 23 December 2022 lists a geographical indication for cua Cà Mau and a collective mark for cua Năm Căn. They are the same crab.

Cá thòi lòi is the mudskipper. Đuông chà là is the palm grub, and not everyone will eat it. Gỏi nhộng ong and lươn um lá nhàu are the U Minh plates. Tôm sú Cà Mau is the province's other geographical indication, and cá chình and cá bống tượng share one Tân Thành mark.

spots.name: Ca thoi loi
spots.note: The mudskipper of the flats, not bony and not strongly fishy. Order it grilled, in a hotpot, braised with pepper, or dried.

spots.name: Duong cha la
spots.note: The fat, white grub of the chà là palm trunk, eaten with nước mắm. Not everyone will try it.

spots.name: Goi nhong ong
spots.note: Young bee pupae from the U Minh honey harvest, best known mixed with banana blossom. The same pupae also come batter-fried or as mắm ong.

spots.name: Luon um la nhau
spots.note: Freshwater eel braised with nhàu leaves and coconut. The eel is sweet, the coconut rich, and the leaves sweet-bitter.

spots.name: Tom su Ca Mau
spots.note: The province's black tiger prawn, protected by a geographical indication alongside cua Cà Mau.

spots.name: Ca chinh and ca bong tuong
spots.nameVi: Cá chình và cá bống tượng Tân Thành
spots.note: Freshwater eel and marble goby sold under one Tân Thành collective trademark.

sections.heading: Seafood and the forest pot
paragraphs: Nghêu Khai Long is the clam from after Tết through the end of May and June. Lẩu mắm U Minh and cá lóc nướng belong to the melaleuca forest. Lẩu cá khoai is the fish hotpot with herbs and bún. Cá khoai Cái Đôi Vàm is the same fish dried, from that town.

spots.name: Ngheu Khai Long
spots.note: Thick, sand-free clams steamed over lemongrass and crushed ginger, eaten hot with muối tiêu chanh. The flat is busiest after Tết through May and June.

spots.name: Lau mam U Minh
spots.note: The fermented-fish hotpot of the forest, shared with fish and forest greens in the pot. One recipe adds shrimp, squid, and lemongrass; another cooks freshwater fish in coconut water.

spots.name: Ca loc nuong
spots.note: Snakehead grilled over straw or tràm-wood charcoal and eaten with forest greens. It is best from the tenth lunar month through the first.

spots.name: Lau ca khoai
spots.address: Cà Mau city and the coast
spots.note: A hotpot of cá khoai, a fish with few bones and crisp, sweet flesh, served with herbs and bún.

spots.name: Ca khoai Cai Doi Vam
spots.address: Thị trấn Cái Đôi Vàm, huyện Phú Tân
spots.note: Dried cá khoai from the drying village of this coastal town, a collective trademark to carry home.

spots.name: Ca kho boi U Minh
spots.note: Dried sặc rằn from a fish that grows slowly here. The dried flesh is firm and fragrant.

spots.name: Mam ca loc Thoi Binh
spots.note: Fermented snakehead from north of the city, a collective trademark and a gift to carry home.

spots.name: Tom kho Rach Goc
spots.note: Dried mangrove shrimp under the Rạch Gốc collective mark. Eat it with rice or carry a bag home.

sections.heading: Sweets and bags
paragraphs: Mật ong U Minh is the jar. Bánh phồng tôm is the cracker from Năm Căn, also sold under the Mũi Cà Mau mark. Chuối khô Trần Hợi, dưa bồn bồn Cái Nước, and rượu trái giác are the other gifts.

spots.name: Mat ong U Minh
spots.note: Melaleuca honey taken from gác kèo ong, the rafters set up to draw the bees. Eat it by the spoon or carry a jar home.

spots.name: Banh phong tom
spots.note: The shrimp cracker of the fishing town on the road to the cape, a crisp snack and a bag to carry.

spots.name: Bon bon Cai Nuoc
spots.note: Pickled bồn bồn, the cattail of Cái Nước. Eat it with rice or carry a jar home.

spots.name: Chuoi kho Tran Hoi
spots.note: Dried banana under the Trần Hợi collective mark, the sweet on the gift list.

spots.name: Ruou trai giac
spots.note: A spirit made from giác fruit, on the Cà Mau list of gifts to carry home.

sections.heading: A ride away
paragraphs: Cần Thơ is the previous stop on the expressway, and its dawn market is a different river. Do not order a Cần Thơ, Bến Tre, or Châu Đốc recipe and call it this cape.

seoTitle: Ca Mau food guide — crab, ba khia, and the cape menu
seoDescription: What to eat in Ca Mau: mangrove crab, salted ba khía with rice, mudskipper, U Minh eel and bee-pupa salad, and the dried shrimp, crackers, and honey to carry home.
